{{Quote|Ithorians. Four throats. Quite powerful."<br />"So I've heard.|[[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]] and [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] after witnessing [[Roron Corobb/Legends|Roron Corobb]] destroy a corridor with his voice|<ref name="CW24">{{CW|24}}</ref>}}
'''Ithorians''' were a [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]] [[Diet/Legends|herbivorous]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]]. They were commonly called "[[Hammerhead/Legends|Hammerheads]]" by less sensitive beings because of their long, curving neck and T-shaped head. They found this nickname offensive.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Ithorian_Jedi_FDSS.png|thumb|left|An Ithorian Jedi]]
{{Quote|I was such a promising pupa. Glassy-eyed, appendageless, able to move my body at will. The world was a titillating surface, an endless, glistening horizon that I had only to track across, to let slip under my underbelly, to feel satisfied. Ah, the joys of youth!|[[Unidentified Ithorian (Rimbaux Four)|An Ithorian's]] notes|<ref name="MOAI" />}}
Ithorians had two mouths and four throats, allowing them to speak in stereo. Female Ithorians had two humps on the back of their head, while males had only one. They had glossy, usually brown flesh. They stood roughly between 1.8 to 2.3 meters from [[Ommatophora|eyestalk]] to toe. Their reflexes and coordination were somewhat slower than that of average [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]].

In addition to allowing them to speak their unique stereophonic language, the Ithorians' four throats also had the ability to violently expel air, resulting in a deafening and potentially concussive scream. Although even common Ithorians possessed this strange talent, those with [[The Force|Force]] training (such as [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Roron Corobb/Legends|Roron Corobb]]) could [[Force bellow|push enough power]] into their sonic bellow to shatter iron and shred [[Plasteel/Legends|plasteel]]. Despite this fact, most Ithorians went their entire lives without ever resorting to violence, and so the ability remained relatively ambiguous.

Ithorian youths were known as "[[Pupa/Legends|pupa]]," and were commonly glassy-eyed, appendageless and limber, until they metamorphosized. After the molt, Ithorians lost an [[aural flap]] and every [[locomotion tube]], gained lumps, craters in their [[Bone/Legends|craniums]] and an appetite for [[Ant-fly|ant-flies]]. An adult Ithorian could father several thousand offspring.<ref name="MOAI" />

==History==
{{Quote|The word for love in one language is the word for dinner in others.|[[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]]|audio=IthorianProverb.flac|<ref name="Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>}}
Ithorians were natives of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]], a lush world with sprawling rain forests. The Ithorians [[Ithorian religion|worshipped]] [[Mother Jungle/Legends|Mother Jungle]], and long ago vowed never to desecrate their planet. Once they discovered [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] technology, the Ithorians built expansive "[[Ithorian Herdship|herdships]]" floating in the skies above their homeworld. The species migrated to these platforms, ensuring that Ithor would remain pristine forever. These herdships eventually were given the ability to travel interstellar distances. The Ithorian people were led by their [[High Priest/Legends|high priest]]. First contact with the Republic occurred in [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000 BBY]].

<div style="float:right">[[File:Ithorian_senators.png|thumb|left|220px|The Ithorian delegation in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]]]</div>

Abroad, Ithorians integrated well with the [[Galactic community]]. Their own language was incredibly beautiful, yet difficult to learn, as the Ithorians had twin mouths on opposite sides of their necks. Fortunately, they could speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], albeit with a strange accent. Many ithorians also used translation devices such as the [[Translator collar/Legends|Ithorian translator]], which was usualy mounted on top of their elongated neck. Each Ithorian herd was presided over by a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] individual who served as both a priest and healer.

The Ithorians were crucial to the efforts to restore many planets that had been devastated by the [[Mandalorian Wars|Mandalorian]] and [[Jedi Civil War]]s. One notable example was [[Telos IV]], whose [[Telosian Restoration Project|reconstruction]] was minutely directed and supervised by [[Chodo Habat]] and his [[Chodo Habat's herd|herd]].

Around the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], a proxy conflict between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], it was discovered that the previously unknown [[Species/Legends|species]] responsible for building the technological wonder that were the [[Heffrin Aqueducts]] on the planet [[Heffrin]], were in fact early Ithorian [[Scout/Legends|explorers]]. This led to great debate among the Ithorian culture.<ref name="The Aqueducts of Haffrin">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Archaeology|The Aqueducts of Haffrin}}</ref>

Ithorian society maintained its peaceful nature by exiling those who had a tendency towards violence and aggression. Two such exiles were the [[Moomo Brothers|Moomo brothers]], [[Dob Moomo|Dob]] and [[Del Moomo|Del]], who worked for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] as hired muscle, although they were less than competent in their efforts. An exile named [[Momaw Nadon/Legends|Momaw Nadon]] was present in the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] cantina shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Ithor was destroyed by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] as part of their invasion plan. They chose to destroy this planet, even though it was a lush jungle world, because [[Bafforr tree|one of the trees]]' pollen could cause their [[Vonduun Skerr Kyrric|Vonduun Crab Armor]] to expand rapidly, killing the [[Warrior caste|Warrior]]. Many years after the Yuuzhan Vong invasion, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] convinced [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Cal Omas]] to allow the Ithorians to resettle on the planet [[Borao]] in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] over [[RePlanetHab]], a large reconstruction conglomerate. Other Ithorians settled on [[Öetrago/Legends|Öetrago]], [[Upell]] and [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]].

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|For every plant that was destroyed in the harvest, two must be planted to replace it|[[Momaw Nadon/Legends|Momaw Nadon]] reciting the Ithorian's "[[Law of Life]]"|<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ithorian_TOR.jpg|thumb|left|150px|An Ithorian]]
Ithorians worshipped the "[[Mother Jungle/Legends|Mother Jungle]]," a spiritual entity embodying the lush, tropical ecology of their world, [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]]. They were generally devoted environmentalists, staunch herbivores, and complete pacifists, devoting much time to contemplating their ecology, studying plants and their uses and the overall respecting of all living things. Most Ithorians hardly set foot on their own planet, instead living in floating cities above their world called herdships. Only three of their continents had been explored and harvested, the other two remain untouched by Ithorian hands. This demonstrated their extreme belief in the protection and sustaining of their environment which was apparent through their "Law of Life."

The Ithorians were organized into [[Ithorian herd/Legends|herds]],<ref name="Starfaring Jungles">{{GamerCite|4|Starfaring Jungles}}</ref> or clan families,<ref name="FF122">{{FactFile|122|ITH 1-2|Ithorian Herd Ships}}</ref> which were the principal social group of the Ithorian society.<ref name="Starfaring Jungles" />

The Ithorians practiced a communal form of government. Each herdship was autonomous and self-supporting. However once every Ithorian season (about five standard years), the herds gathered for a [[Herd Meet/Legends|Herd meet]], a grand gathering above the surface of their world, where the herd ships would join each other in a festival and regal ceremony. Within Ithorian society, there were a priestly group known as [[nature priest]]s who communed with the "Mother Jungle" and had a deeper connection to the Ithorian homeworld. Within the trading guilds themselves, [[Merchantate]]s were present who dealt with business matters.

The Ithorian's curious and gregarious nature meant that many found their way off-planet via their floating herdship's space-worthy counterparts. Many became galactic traders, traveling the stars either independently or as part of their herdship. They would only resort to violence if threatened, and they were more likely to use their sonic bellow than a weapon. Because of their mild demeanor, most Ithorians avoided war in general, although the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] did boast a few among its ranks. Their pacifistic nature meant that they refused to touch things that came as a result of bloodshed. When dealing with others, Ithorians were always supremely polite. They were very conversational and had profound respect for the views of others. Though often described as likable and friendly, many sentients found them altogether dull. Even when they had disagreements, Ithorians were unlikely to discuss their grievances with anyone unless the offending party was present. To do otherwise was considered rude.

[[File:Ithorian-NEGAS.png|thumb|right|180px|An Ithorian tending to plant life]]
Ithorians were commonly named after creatures on their planet, such as the [[Flen]] and [[Gillom]]. Many females were named after the [[Cellwan]], [[Haali]], [[Ivuur]], [[Oovei]], [[Vonnuvi]], and [[Wimmel]]; many males were named after the [[Boolon]], [[Murr]], [[Neelig]], and [[Waawat]]. Aamaw, meaning "firelight", was also a very common name.<ref name="GCG">''[[Galactic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Other examples of Ithorian names included Fandomar, Momaw, Oraltor, and Trangle.<ref name="SWRPGCore">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

In Ithorian [[mythology]] [[Trinta (Ithorian mythology)|Trinta]] was the realm of [[Demon/Legends|demons]]. The Ithorians named the planet [[Trinta]] after this realm because they disliked the planet.<ref name="DoE">''[[Domain of Evil]]''</ref>

==Ithorians in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Never pass up an opportunity to trade with an Ithorian. You'll get high-quality goods, and unless you really let him gouge you, you'll get a fair price.|''The Spacer's Handbook'' (Bootleg Edition)|<ref name="GG9">''[[Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim]]''</ref>}}
Practicing their gentle nature even when offworld, many Ithorians served as explorers, diplomats, peace officers and navigators. Despite their reputation, not all Ithorians were so peaceful. Rarely, violent and unruly Ithorians were born and subsequently banished from their homeworld or herdship. Such Ithorians often became drifters and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], like [[Del Moomo|Del]] and [[Dob Moomo]].

On some poor worlds where Ithorians had established trading centers, Ithorians were happy to give produce away to impoverished locals. Ithorians also pioneered several crop education programs for produce growers on poor and uneducated planets.<ref name="GG9" />

Many Ithorians were Force-sensitive and went on to serve the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], as the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]] valued the good nature that Ithorians so cherished.

==Behind the scenes==
The Ithorian puppet suit used in the Mos Eisley cantina scene of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] was designed by [[Ron Cobb]]. This puppet was used for Momaw Nadon and [[Deneb Both]]. Interestingly, it featured four fingers on each hand, while later Ithorian designs, such as Roron Corobb and [[Tendau Bendon/Legends|Tendau Bendon]] (both of whom appear chronologically before Nadon and Both) feature five-fingered hands. Most sources other than Cobb's puppet, including ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', seem to favor the five-fingered design.

In the [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] commented on seeing a '''Meerian Hammerhead''' while in the cantina. Since then, another species has been identified as [[Meerian/Legends|Meerians]].
